title: $6.3 Billion Stolen in 20 Minutes: How the Biggest Crypto Hack Ever Happened
description:
On October 29, 2026, hackers drained about $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, in about 20 minutes. It's the largest crypto theft ever recorded, roughly four times the old record. Here's how it happened, who the FBI says did it, who pays for it, and what it means for anyone who keeps money on an exchange.

What we know (as of November 1, 2026):
- Binance's first findings: a compromised engineer's laptop gave access to a service container; Binance says it found no evidence its private keys leaked; its co-CEO says the attack was more complex
- TRM Labs: staging began well before the theft; signatures obtained in advance, executed in one burst
- FBI (Oct 31): North Korea is responsible (a group known as TraderTraitor); funds are being converted mostly into Ethereum
- About $3 billion frozen with partners including Tether and Circle (Binance)
- Binance says it will absorb the losses (SAFU fund, futures insurance fund, treasury): about 90% covered Saturday, 95% Sunday
- Withdrawals resumed in phases on November 1

Details may still change; Binance says a full incident report will follow.
